# StaleGuard

> Silent stale-build detection for React apps. Two recipes: Vite + static host, and Next.js App Router (self-hosted). Reload on tab focus — no banners, no polling.

The site UI is a client-rendered SPA. Hash routes such as `#/implementation` are not sent to the server, so tools that only fetch HTML cannot read those pages. Use the plain-text resources below instead.

## Recipes (start here)

- [Vite + static host — agent guide](AGENT_GUIDE.md): Three files, `index.html` ETag / Last-Modified, Azure SWA cache header
- [Next.js App Router (self-hosted)](docs/nextjs-app-router.md): `/api/version`, focus hook, `NEXT_DEPLOYMENT_ID`, Docker — full guide for agents and developers
- [Full documentation export](llms-full.txt): All doc pages in one file for single-request ingestion

## Doc pages (site walkthrough)

- [How it works](docs/how-it-works.md): Flow from deploy to silent reload (Vite-oriented demo)
- [Vite recipe](docs/implementation.md): Three-file setup overview (links to the agent guide for full snippets)
- [Edge cases](docs/edge-cases.md): Failure modes and how the hook handles them

## Source and repository

- [README](https://github.com/trivedi-vatsal/StaleGuard/blob/main/README.md): Local dev, hosting, and testing
- [useVersionCheck.ts](https://github.com/trivedi-vatsal/StaleGuard/blob/main/src/hooks/useVersionCheck.ts): Demo hook (Vite recipe) with diagnostics support
- [staticwebapp.config.json](https://github.com/trivedi-vatsal/StaleGuard/blob/main/public/staticwebapp.config.json): Azure SWA cache header for index.html

## Optional
